subject: Computer Engineering Laws and Discipline
org: ACES - Association of Computer Engineering Students of STI Ortigas-Cainta
description: Prelim to finals reviewer covering computer engineering law, ethics, professionalism, contemporary issues, and the CPE profession.
license: For ACES classroom use only. Handout content is property of STI.

handouts.title: Introduction to CPE Laws and Professional Practice
Analysis of the Current Computer Engineering & IT Field Using Case Study
Application of IT Laws in the Computer Engineering Field

questions.stem: Under CHED's policies, what does the Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering program embody?
options: The study of business processes and accounting information systems
The science and technology of design, development, implementation, maintenance, and integration of software and hardware components in modern computing systems and computer-controlled equipment
Only the repair and maintenance of computer hardware and networks
The legal regulation of cybercrime and data privacy in the Philippines
questions.explanation: The handout defines BSCpE as embodying the science and technology of design, development, implementation, maintenance, and integration of software and hardware components in modern computing systems and computer-controlled equipment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the difference between computer engineers and computer scientists in hardware?
options: Computer engineers only repair hardware, while computer scientists design every processor
Both professions avoid working with hardware
Computer scientists build hardware, while computer engineers only write software
Computer engineers build hardware, while computer scientists generally do not
questions.explanation: In hardware, computer engineers build hardware while computer scientists generally do not, although computer scientists know enough about hardware to analyze system operations and interact with hardware engineers.

questions.stem: In software, which statement is accurate?
options: Computer scientists know more about the theory of computation, programming languages, and operating systems, while computer engineers often work as programmers writing programs for computer-based systems
Computer engineers know more about the theory of computation than computer scientists
Computer engineers never work as programmers
Computer scientists are not allowed to work with operating systems
questions.explanation: In software, computer scientists know more about the underlying theory of computation, programming languages, and operating systems, while computer engineers often work as programmers writing programs for computer-based systems.

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the three characteristics a computer engineer should generally satisfy?
options: Having depth of knowledge in mathematics and engineering sciences
Designing computers, computer-based systems, and networks with both hardware and software subject to trade-offs
Acquiring and maintaining preparation for professional practice in engineering
Passing a government board licensure examination before practice
questions.explanation: The three characteristics are the ability to design computers and systems subject to trade-offs, depth of knowledge in mathematics and engineering sciences, and preparation for professional practice. A board licensure exam is not required for Computer Engineering.

questions.stem: Why must computer engineers be life-long learners?
options: Because the computing field changes rapidly, they must maintain their knowledge and skills within their chosen discipline
Because schools require them to return as students
Because their professional licenses expire every five years
Because hardware and software never change
questions.explanation: Because of the rapid pace of change in the computing field, computer engineers must be life-long learners to maintain their knowledge and skills within their chosen discipline.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a duty of computer engineers?
options: Writing and testing software for mobile devices and computers
Representing clients in court during cybercrime cases
Designing and testing computer hardware components such as processors and circuit boards
Designing, setting up, and testing networks
questions.explanation: The listed duties include researching software and hardware, designing and testing hardware components, writing and testing software, designing and testing networks, managing operating systems, designing and testing robots, and creating programs for products. Court representation is not listed.

questions.stem: Professionalism is demonstrated by more than qualifications, knowledge, and skills. What else does it require?
options: Strict adherence to a single employer for life
A board license and a master's degree
questions.explanation: Professionalism is demonstrated by more than just qualifications, knowledge, and skills. It also requires integrity, ethics, and trust.

questions.stem: Which professionalism characteristic means a professional gets the job done well, with abilities that match the role and results that often exceed expectations?
questions.explanation: Competence means the professional gets the job done and done well; abilities match the requirements of the role and often produce results that exceed expectations.

questions.stem: Which professionalism characteristic involves developing detailed, up-to-date, often highly specialized knowledge and putting it into action?
questions.explanation: Knowledge involves developing detailed, up-to-date, often highly specialized knowledge, and being confident enough to put that knowledge into action to help yourself and others succeed.

questions.stem: How is respect demonstrated by a professional?
options: By being a role model of politeness and good manners to everyone, taking people's needs into account, and upholding their rights
questions.explanation: Respect means being a role model for politeness and good manners to everyone, not just people you want to impress. True respect takes other people's needs into account and helps uphold their rights.

questions.stem: Which characteristic is shown by staying professional under pressure and by being aware of other people's feelings?
questions.explanation: Staying professional even under pressure is a sign of a true professional. This takes strategies for managing emotions and a clear awareness of other people's feelings: emotional intelligence.

questions.stem: Which characteristic keeps professionals true to their word and stops them from compromising their values even when the road is harder?
questions.explanation: Integrity keeps professional people true to their word and stops them from compromising their values, even if that means taking a harder road. It is bound up with honesty.

questions.stem: Appropriateness covers outward appearances such as dress, grooming, and body language. What else does it cover?
options: The way you speak and write, the topics you discuss, and how you behave with others
Only the clothes you wear at work
questions.explanation: Appropriateness relates to outward appearances such as dress, grooming, and body language, but it also covers the way you speak and write, the topics you choose to discuss, and how you behave with others.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects conscientiousness?
options: Being reliable, setting high standards, planning and prioritizing work, and holding yourself accountable without letting perfectionism take over
Working longer hours than everyone else and obsessing about details
Taking credit for the team's output
Never asking for help under any circumstance
questions.explanation: Conscientiousness means being reliable, setting your own high standards, showing care about every aspect of the job, and being industrious, organized, and accountable. The handout warns not to confuse it with working longer hours or obsessing over details.

questions.stem: What does well-founded confidence do for a professional?
options: It reassures and motivates others, boosts influence and leadership, and encourages taking on new challenges
It replaces the need for competence and knowledge
It removes the need to listen to feedback
It guarantees that mistakes will never happen
questions.explanation: Well-founded confidence reassures and motivates other people, boosting the ability to influence and lead. It also pushes you to take on new challenges because the fear of damaging your professional reputation is non-existent.

questions.stem: What is cybersecurity?
options: The law that governs the digital dissemination of information and software
The act of selling personal data to advertisers
The process of safeguarding important information from corruption, compromise, or loss
The practice of protecting systems, networks, and programs from digital attacks
questions.explanation: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting systems, networks, and programs from digital attacks. It has enormous implications for government security, economic prosperity, and public safety.

questions.stem: What is data protection?
options: A crime committed using information and communication technologies
The process of safeguarding important information from corruption, compromise, or loss
The acquisition of a domain name in bad faith
questions.explanation: Data protection is the process of safeguarding important information from corruption, compromise, or loss. Its importance grows as the amount of data created and stored continues to increase.

questions.stem: Which best defines cybercrime?
options: A crime that can only be committed by hackers
A crime committed with or using information and communication technologies such as smartphones, computers, and networks
A violation of the Anti-Wiretapping Law only
Any crime committed inside a school
questions.explanation: Cybercrime is a crime committed with or using information and communication technologies such as radio, television, smartphones, computers and networks, and other communication devices.

questions.stem: Which law is the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012?
questions.explanation: The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 is Republic Act No. 10175. It addresses crimes committed against and through computer systems.

questions.stem: Which law aims to facilitate domestic and international agreements, contracts, and electronic transactions while recognizing the authenticity and reliability of electronic documents?
questions.explanation: The E-Commerce Act of 2000 (RA 8792) aims to facilitate domestic and international agreements, contracts, exchanges, and storage of information through electronic means and to promote electronic transactions.

questions.stem: A person fraudulently uses another person's credit card and access device. Which law primarily covers this?
questions.explanation: RA 8484, the Access Device Regulation Act of 1998, regulates the issuance and use of access devices and prohibits fraudulent acts involving them.

questions.stem: Which law prohibits and penalizes wiretapping and other violations of the privacy of communication?
questions.explanation: RA 4200, the Anti-Wiretapping Law, prohibits and penalizes wiretapping and other related violations of the privacy of communication.

questions.stem: Which agency administers and implements the Data Privacy Act of 2012?
questions.explanation: The Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173) protects individual personal information in ICT systems. The National Privacy Commission administers and implements its provisions and ensures compliance with international standards.

questions.stem: Which law defines and penalizes child pornography and promotes the well-being of the youth?
questions.explanation: RA 9775, the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009, defines the crime of child pornography, prescribes penalties, and promotes the physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual, emotional, psychological, and social well-being of the youth.

questions.stem: Which law penalizes taking or broadcasting photos or videos of a person performing a sexual act without consent?
questions.explanation: RA 9995, the Anti-Photo and Voyeurism Act of 2009, penalizes photo and video voyeurism, including selling, reproducing, or broadcasting such recordings without written consent.

questions.stem: Accessing the whole or any part of a computer system without right is called:
questions.explanation: Illegal access refers to access to the whole or any part of a computer system without right. It is an offense against the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of computer data and systems.

questions.stem: Which offense refers to intercepting, by technical means and without right, any non-public transmission of computer data to, from, or within a computer system?
questions.explanation: Illegal interception is the interception, by technical means and without right, of any non-public transmission of computer data to, from, or within a computer system, including electromagnetic emissions carrying such data.

questions.stem: Which offense involves intentionally or recklessly altering, damaging, deleting, or deteriorating computer data without right, including introducing viruses?
questions.explanation: Data interference refers to the intentional or reckless alteration, damaging, deletion, or deterioration of computer data, electronic documents, or electronic data messages without right, including the introduction or transmission of viruses.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Budapest Convention is correct?
options: It is the first international treaty on crimes committed via the Internet and other computer networks, drawn up by the Council of Europe in Strasbourg in November 2001
It is a Philippine law enacted in 2012 to punish cybercrime
It is a United Nations treaty that only covers copyright infringement
It is a Caribbean project for harmonizing ICT policies
questions.explanation: The Convention on Cybercrime (Treaty #185, Budapest Convention) is the first international treaty on crimes committed via the Internet and other computer networks. It was drawn up by the Council of Europe in Strasbourg, France, in November 2001.

questions.stem: What was the first recorded cybercrime in the Philippines?
options: The 'I Love You' virus released by Onel de Guzman in 2000, which was initially dismissed because no law punished cybercrimes at the time
questions.explanation: The first recorded cybercrime in the Philippines was in 2000 when Onel de Guzman released the 'I Love You' virus. It was dismissed at first because there was no law punishing cybercrimes at the time.

questions.stem: Who accused Senator Risa Hontiveros of violating the anti-wiretapping law in 2017?
options: Former Negros Oriental representative Jacinto 'Jing' Paras
Former Justice Secretary Vitaliano Aguirre II
questions.explanation: On September 12, 2017, former Negros Oriental representative Jacinto 'Jing' Paras said that Senator Risa Hontiveros was liable for wiretapping during a privilege speech at the Senate.

questions.stem: What did Hontiveros present during her privilege speech that led to the wiretapping complaint?
options: A photo of a text exchange between Aguirre and a 'CongJing'
A recording of a phone call
A screenshot of a GCash phishing site
A copy of the COMELEC database
questions.explanation: Hontiveros presented a photo at the Senate showing Aguirre texting a 'CongJing', later assumed to be Jacinto Paras, during a Senate probe about the extrajudicial killing of Kian delos Santos.

questions.stem: Which law was cited in the complaint against Hontiveros?
questions.explanation: Paras argued that Hontiveros' action violated the Anti-Wiretapping Law, Republic Act No. 4200.

questions.stem: How much bail did Hontiveros post after the arrest order in December 2021?
questions.explanation: Hontiveros posted bail of PHP36,000 after the release of the arrest order against her, calling the case 'worthless and baseless'.

questions.stem: In the December 2021 BDO hacking incident, funds were transferred to the UnionBank account of which name?
questions.explanation: BDO users complained about illegal transactions transferring money to the UnionBank account of a certain 'Mark Nagoyo'.

questions.stem: Which laws were cited against the BDO hacking suspects?
options: Anti-Wiretapping Law and Data Privacy Act
Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998 and Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012
Anti-Child Pornography Act and the Revised Penal Code only
E-Commerce Act and Anti-Photo and Voyeurism Act
questions.explanation: The NBI charged the suspects with violating the Access Devices Regulation Act of 1998 and the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

questions.stem: Who acted as a 'verifier,' pretending to conduct a survey and asking victims for identification cards in exchange for PHP50 in prepaid credit?
questions.explanation: Panaligan acted as a verifier, pretending to conduct a survey and asking victims for IDs with photographs in exchange for PHP50 in prepaid credit. The information was used to apply for verified GCash or PayMaya accounts.

questions.stem: Who was found selling a 'SCAMPAGE,' a phishing website imitating GCash, for PHP2,000?
questions.explanation: Taupa was found selling a 'SCAMPAGE' for PHP2,000. It was a phishing website imitating GCash, used to harvest login details, usernames, passwords, and MPINs.

questions.stem: Who was suspected of hacking the COMELEC website and data in 2016?
options: Paul Loui Biteng, a 20-year-old IT graduate
questions.explanation: Paul Loui Biteng, a 20-year-old Information Technology graduate, faced charges for allegedly hacking into the COMELEC website and data.

questions.stem: Which violations were filed against the suspected COMELEC hacker?
options: Illegal access to a computer system, data interference, and misuse of devices
Child pornography, voyeurism, and identity theft
questions.explanation: Chief Inquest Prosecutor Atty. Jovencio Senados said there was enough evidence for several violations of the cybercrime prevention law: illegal access to a computer system, data interference, and misuse of devices.

questions.stem: How many Filipino voters' personal information was exposed in the COMELEC data leak?
questions.explanation: The COMELEC incident was labeled as the biggest private data leak in Philippine history, exposing the personal information of 55 million Filipino voters.

questions.stem: What happened to the cybercrime case against the suspected COMELEC hacker?
options: It was dismissed after four years because the prosecution failed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt
He posted PHP36,000 bail and the case continues
The case was dismissed because no cybercrime law existed in 2016
He was convicted and sentenced to 26 months
questions.explanation: Four years later, a Manila court dismissed the cybercrime case against Biteng after the prosecution failed to prove him guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

questions.stem: How many people were charged with cybercrimes related to the pandemic since March 2020, including 52 suspects for spreading fake news?
questions.explanation: Eighty people were charged with various cybercrimes related to the pandemic since March 2020, including 52 suspects spreading fake news about the coronavirus disease.

questions.stem: How much data was claimed to have been extracted and deleted in the ransomware attack on Brazil's Ministry of Health in December 2021?
questions.explanation: The Lapsus$ Group claimed responsibility and said 50TB worth of data had been extracted from the Ministry of Health's systems and subsequently deleted.

questions.stem: What tools did Robert Davies use to infect victims' devices and gain remote access?
questions.explanation: Davies used crypters, software that encrypts malware to bypass security programs, and remote administration tools (RATs) to gain remote access to victims' devices and steal sexual images.

questions.stem: What is a case study?
options: A research methodology involving a detailed and intensive analysis of a particular event, situation, organization, or social unit
An experiment conducted in a controlled laboratory
A survey of a large random sample
A statistical method for predicting population parameters
questions.explanation: A case study is a research methodology that involves a detailed and intensive analysis of a particular event, situation, organization, or social unit. Case studies are best conceptualized by the scope of interest rather than by specific methods.

questions.stem: What is the first step in a problem-oriented case study?
options: Outline the purpose of the case study
questions.explanation: The first step is to outline the purpose of the case study, which serves as a guide and direction as the researchers arrive at a solution.

questions.stem: Which step comes immediately after identifying the problems in a case study?
options: Select the major problems in the case
questions.explanation: After identifying the problems, the next step is to select the major problems in the case. This helps narrow down problems that do not necessarily affect the study directly.

questions.stem: What is the final step in the case study process described in the handout?
questions.explanation: The fifth step is to recommend the best solution. It should cover most of the problems, with details on how it will be applied to conclude the study.

questions.stem: Which is a benefit of case studies?
options: They provide a comprehensive understanding of a bounded unit and allow readers to learn from the case
They guarantee statistically generalizable results for all populations
They always require less data than surveys
They eliminate the need for data analysis
questions.explanation: A case study provides a comprehensive understanding of a bounded unit and helps the reader examine that case so they can learn from it. It also allows transferability, which is different from statistical generalization.

questions.stem: Which is a limitation of case studies?
options: The sheer volume of data can be difficult to organize, and researchers may veer away from the research focus
They cannot use interviews or documents
They cannot be used in the IT field
questions.explanation: Limitations include difficulty organizing the sheer volume of data, the temptation to veer away from the research focus, and challenges in reporting findings from multiple-case studies.

questions.stem: Which type of case study explores differences within and between cases to replicate findings across cases?
questions.explanation: A collective case study enables the researcher to explore differences within and between cases, with the goal of replicating findings across cases. Cases must be chosen carefully to predict related or contrasting results.

questions.stem: Which type of case study answers a question that seeks to explain presumed causal links in real-life interventions too complex for surveys or experiments?
questions.explanation: An explanatory case study is used to answer a question that seeks to explain presumed causal links in real-life interventions that are too complex for survey or experimental strategies.

questions.stem: Which type of case study starts with a descriptive theory, observes subjects, and compares gathered information to the pre-existing theory?
questions.explanation: A descriptive case study starts with a descriptive theory. The subjects are then observed, and the information gathered is compared to the pre-existing theory.

questions.stem: Which type of case study explores situations in which the intervention being evaluated has no clear, single set of outcomes?
questions.explanation: An exploratory case study is used to explore situations in which the intervention being evaluated has no clear, single set of outcomes.

questions.stem: Which type of case study is used to accomplish something other than understanding a particular situation, with the case playing a supportive role to refine a theory?
questions.explanation: An instrumental case study provides insight into an issue or helps refine a theory. The case is of secondary interest and plays a supportive role, facilitating understanding of something else.

questions.stem: John W. Scheib's study on role stress in the professional life of school music teachers is an example of which type?
questions.explanation: The handout gives Scheib's 'Role stress in the professional life of the school music teacher: A collective case study' as an example of a collective case study.

questions.stem: Luiz Joia's study 'Analyzing a Web-based e-commerce community: A case study in Brazil' is an example of which type?
questions.explanation: The handout gives Joia's study on a Web-based e-commerce community in Brazil as an example of an explanatory case study.

questions.stem: The STAMP study by Lauretta Luck on observable behavior indicating potential patient violence is an example of which type?
questions.explanation: The STAMP study by Lauretta Luck, Debra Jackson, and Kim User is given as an example of an instrumental case study.

questions.stem: Which is a significance of case studies in the CPE/IT field?
options: They guarantee that every IT project will succeed
They eliminate the need for theories and hypotheses
They help professionals and students understand field behaviors, find causes and solutions, answer complicated questions, and give direction to technical advances
They replace all technical research and development
questions.explanation: Case studies in CPE/IT help understand behaviors in the field, find causes and solutions to specific events, answer complicated questions that simple research and sampling cannot solve, and give clearer direction to technical advances.

questions.stem: What is ethics?
options: The study of computer hardware and software
The analysis of human actions from the perspective of 'good' and 'evil,' or 'morally correct' and 'morally wrong'
The set of laws enacted by the government
The process of protecting systems from digital attacks
questions.explanation: Ethics is defined as the analysis of human actions from the perspective of 'good' and 'evil,' or 'morally correct' and 'morally wrong.' It is concerned with rights, responsibilities, language, living an ethical life, and moral decisions.

questions.stem: Why do computer engineers have ethical responsibilities that go beyond complying with laws?
options: Because they are required to pass a board exam
Because laws do not apply to computer engineers
Their decisions affect the performance and functionality of computer systems, which directly affect the welfare of users
questions.explanation: Ethical responsibilities are tasks computer engineers are obligated to perform meticulously because their decisions affect system performance and functionality, which in turn directly affect the welfare of users. These obligations go beyond complying with laws or regulations.

questions.stem: Which ethical responsibility affirms an obligation to protect fundamental human rights, respect cultural diversity, and minimize negative consequences of computing systems?
options: Contribute to society and human well-being
Give proper credit for intellectual property
questions.explanation: Contributing to society and human well-being affirms an obligation to protect fundamental human rights and respect the diversity of all cultures. An essential aim is to minimize negative consequences of computing systems, including threats to health and safety.

questions.stem: In computing ethics, what does 'harm' include?
options: Only physical injury to a person
Injury or negative consequences such as loss of information, loss of property, property damage, or unwanted environmental impacts
Only financial loss caused by fraud
questions.explanation: Harm means injury or negative consequences, such as undesirable loss of information, loss of property, property damage, or unwanted environmental impacts to users, the public, employees, and employers.

questions.stem: Which ethical responsibility requires not taking credit for others' ideas or work even when the work is not explicitly protected by copyright or patent?
options: Be fair and act not to discriminate
Give proper credit for intellectual property
questions.explanation: It is an obligation to protect the integrity of intellectual property. One must not take credit for others' ideas or work, even when the work has not been explicitly protected by copyright, patent, or similar protections.

questions.stem: Which practice best respects the privacy of others?
options: Collect only necessary personal information, clearly define retention and disposal periods, and do not use it for other purposes without consent
Share data with advertisers to fund the system
Collect as much data as possible in case it becomes useful
Keep personal data indefinitely to avoid losing records
questions.explanation: Respecting privacy includes maintaining the privacy and integrity of personal data, ensuring accuracy, protecting it from unauthorized access, collecting only necessary information, defining retention and disposal periods, and not using it for other purposes without consent.

questions.stem: What does the ethical responsibility to be honest and trustworthy require?
options: Hiding system limitations to protect the company's reputation
Not making deliberately false or deceptive claims about a system, disclosing limitations and problems, and being honest about qualifications and conflicts of interest
questions.explanation: An honest professional will not make deliberately false or deceptive claims about a system or system design but will provide full disclosure of suitable system limitations and problems. They also have a duty to be honest about their qualifications and conflicts of interest.

questions.stem: Which ethical responsibility prohibits discrimination based on race, sex, religion, age, disability, national origin, or similar factors?
options: Be fair and act not to discriminate
Give proper credit for intellectual property
Contribute to society and human well-being
questions.explanation: Discrimination based on race, sex, religion, age, disability, national origin, or other such factors leads to inequities that may result from the use or misuse of information and technology.

questions.stem: What do professional responsibilities of computer engineers mainly deal with?
options: How they act and behave within a company or organization, including relationships with co-workers
questions.explanation: Professional responsibilities deal with how computer engineers act and behave within the bounds of a company or organization, including the relationship with their co-workers.

questions.stem: Which professional responsibility states that excellence is the most important obligation of a professional, and poor quality can have serious negative consequences?
options: Strive to achieve the highest quality, effectiveness, and dignity
questions.explanation: Excellence is the most important obligation of a professional. They must strive to achieve quality and be aware of the serious negative consequences that may result from poor quality in a system.

questions.stem: Which activities are listed as ways to acquire and maintain professional competence?
options: Only earning a single college degree
Independent study, attending seminars or conferences or courses, and involvement in professional organizations
questions.explanation: Upgrading technical knowledge and competence can be achieved through independent study; attending seminars, conferences, or courses; and being involved in professional organizations.

questions.stem: Which professional responsibility includes accepting personal accountability for professional work, with ethical judgment as the final guide?
options: Honor contracts, agreements, and assigned responsibilities
questions.explanation: Honoring commitments is a matter of integrity and honesty. The major underlying principle is the obligation to accept personal accountability for professional work, and the computing professional's ethical judgment should be the final guide.

questions.stem: Which social responsibility area focuses on protecting public safety, health, and welfare, such as robots for the elderly and sensors for gas leaks?
questions.explanation: Human safety is a primary duty to protect public safety, health, and welfare. Examples include robotics that target automation for elderly people and sensors that detect dangers such as gas leaks or chemicals.

questions.stem: Which social responsibility area involves proper disposal of electronic waste and developing machines that separate waste or improve the quality of life of animals and trees?
questions.explanation: Environment and sustainability addresses electronic waste. It is the responsibility of computer engineers and computing professionals to dispose of devices and e-waste correctly and to develop smart machines that separate waste or improve life for animals and trees.

questions.stem: What does 'pro bono publico' mean, and what does it require of computer engineers?
options: It means 'by law'; engineers must only follow legal requirements
It means 'without technology'; engineers should avoid computing
It means 'for the public good'; engineers should share technical expertise with individuals or organizations unable to access or pay for them
It means 'for profit'; engineers should prioritize paid work
questions.explanation: Pro bono publico is a Latin term meaning 'for the public good.' Computer engineers have a duty to share technical expertise and knowledge with individuals and organizations unable to access or pay for them, such as through outreach programs and trainings.

questions.stem: Which set lists the five principles of professionalism in the workplace?
options: Leadership, interpersonal, self-management, problem solving, and open-mindedness
Competence, knowledge, respect, integrity, and confidence
Planning, organizing, staffing, directing, and controlling
Communication, teamwork, critical thinking, ethics, and humanness
questions.explanation: The five principles are communication, teamwork, critical thinking, ethics, and humanness. The second option lists some core professionalism characteristics, and the last option lists professional skills.

questions.stem: Which principle emphasizes verbal and body language, e-etiquette, and the resources needed to develop communication skills?
questions.explanation: Communication covers verbal, body language, e-etiquette, and more. Quality communication can eliminate unnecessary problems, promote better performance, increase productivity, and create a strong team.

questions.stem: Which principle builds strong employee relationships and helps eliminate a toxic work culture characterized by drama, fighting, low morale, and lack of communication?
questions.explanation: Teamwork builds strong employee relationships. One benefit is that it eliminates toxic work culture, which is characterized by drama, fighting, low morale at work, lack of communication, and the boss's fear.

questions.stem: Which principle allows a person to analyze information, arrive at conclusions, and make sound decisions, and helps connect ideas and evaluate arguments?
questions.explanation: Critical thinking allows a person to analyze information, arrive at conclusions, and make sound decisions. It enhances communication, creativity, problem-solving, and the ability to connect ideas, evaluate arguments, find errors, and solve complex issues.

questions.stem: Which principle aligns employee behavior, fosters openness, partnership, and trust, and helps employees feel secure when supervisors treat them with respect?
questions.explanation: An organization that introduces a workplace ethics program aligns employee behavior and fosters openness, partnership, and trust. Employees perform better when they know supervisors' expectations and feel secure because there is no harassment and supervisors treat them with respect.

questions.stem: Which principle is expressed through innate human values, unique talents, purpose, growth, work-life balance, kindness, and emotional availability?
questions.explanation: Humanness is expressed through innate human values and unique talents and perspectives. Humanity is dynamic and encompasses the natural need for purpose, growth, and work-life balance. Practicing kindness, acceptance, and emotional availability is a huge step toward humanness.

questions.stem: Which list contains the professional skills employers look for according to Indeed.com?
options: Leadership, interpersonal, self-management, problem solving, and open-mindedness
Communication, teamwork, critical thinking, ethics, and humanness
Competence, knowledge, respect, emotional intelligence, and integrity
Programming, networking, database administration, web development, and cybersecurity
questions.explanation: The professional skills listed are leadership skills, interpersonal skills, self-management skills, problem-solving skills, and open-mindedness. The first option lists the five workplace principles.

questions.stem: Which leadership skill is described as one of the characteristics a good leader should have, with the warning that exploding in rage or screaming at teammates creates a negative environment?
questions.explanation: Emotional intelligence is one of the characteristics a good leader should have. A leader who explodes in rage or screams at teammates only generates a negative environment.

questions.stem: Which skill involves building good relationships, understanding family, friends, coworkers, and clients, and showing real interest in teammates' lives while acknowledging their expertise?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal skills are important for communicating and working with groups and individuals. People with strong interpersonal skills build good relationships and work well with others. The best practice is showing real interest in teammates' lives while acknowledging their expertise.

questions.stem: Which skill allows people to control their thoughts, feelings, and actions to maximize productivity and achieve professional goals?
questions.explanation: Self-management skills are the abilities that allow people to control their thoughts, feelings, and actions. They allow professionals to maximize productivity, improve workplace performance, and efficiently achieve professional goals.

questions.stem: Which skill helps a professional accept technological changes and new ideas without taking them personally, and can be enhanced by reading books and listening to podcasts about other cultures?
questions.explanation: Open-mindedness is important because workplaces are filled with people from different backgrounds, cultures, and life experiences. An open-minded professional also accepts technological changes and new ideas about how to perform a job without taking it personally.

questions.stem: Which list contains the major workplace challenges discussed in the handout?
options: Competence, knowledge, respect, integrity, and confidence
Communication challenges, low employee motivation, difficult people, lack of skill development, and mental health challenges
Hardware failures, software bugs, network outages, power cuts, and viruses
Low salaries, long commutes, food quality, parking, and dress codes
questions.explanation: The major challenges are communication challenges, low employee motivation, difficult people, lack of skill development and professional growth, and mental health challenges.

questions.stem: How does the handout suggest handling 'difficult people' at work?
options: Ignore them completely until they resign
If the conflict gets out of hand, reach out to HR or the person in charge; if manageable, communicate and acknowledge each other's feelings; be kind
Match their negativity so they stop
questions.explanation: If the conflict gets out of hand, reach out to HR or anyone in charge. If the issue is manageable, communicate with one another, understand and acknowledge each other's feelings, and be kind.

questions.stem: Why is lack of skill development and professional growth a challenge, and what is the suggested response?
options: Skills never change, so employees should wait for the company to require training
Training is unnecessary if the employee has a degree
Only managers need training; employees should focus on overtime
Employees risk becoming irrelevant or outdated; they should seek trainings and seminars and take the first steps themselves
questions.explanation: Skill enhancement is essential to improve performance, especially to keep pace with new technology. Otherwise, employees risk becoming irrelevant or outdated. Employees should seek trainings and seminars that cater to their needs and take the first steps themselves.

questions.stem: What does the handout say about mental health challenges at work?
options: Mental health is unrelated to work
Employees should never take time off
A negative working environment, harassment, and bullying can harm mental health and lead to depression and anxiety; taking time off and developing a personal space outside work are important
Only physical health matters in the workplace
questions.explanation: Work is good for mental health, but a negative working environment can lead to physical and mental health problems. Harassment and bullying can have a substantial adverse impact and may lead to depression and anxiety. Taking time off and developing a personal space outside work are important.

questions.stem: What is true about Computer Engineering as a profession in the Philippines?
options: It requires passing the Computer Engineering Licensure Exam before practice
It does not require passing a board licensure exam, so graduates can immediately enter the professional world, but they are still expected to take certifications and trainings
Only graduates with a master's degree may practice
questions.explanation: Computer Engineering does not require studying and passing a Board Licensure Exam, so graduates can immediately enter the professional world. However, graduates are still expected to improve their portfolios by taking additional certifications and trainings accredited by legitimate organizations.

questions.stem: According to DOLE's 2019 Labor Market Trends, what rank and average monthly salary did Computer Engineering have among top-paying jobs?
options: 7th, with an average of PHP49,335 per month
1st, with an average of PHP119,560 per month
6th, with an average of PHP30,000 per month
5th, with an average of PHP49,335 per month
questions.explanation: As per DOLE's 2019 Issue of Labor Market Trends, Computer Engineering ranks 7th among top-paying jobs in the Philippines, with an average of PHP49,335 estimated monthly salary. Computer Programmers and System Analyst and Designers ranked 5th and 6th.

questions.stem: According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics as of 2020, what was the average yearly pay for computer engineers in the US?
questions.explanation: In the US, an average of $119,560 or PHP6,147,476 is expected for computer engineers yearly, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics as of 2020.

questions.stem: What growth does the BLS project for computer engineering from 2019 to 2029 compared with other computer-related jobs?
options: 8% for computer engineering, compared with 22% for others
4% for computer engineering, compared with 2% for others
22% for computer engineering, compared with 8% for others
2% growth for computer engineering, compared with 4% for other computer-related jobs
questions.explanation: The BLS projects 2% growth for computer engineering from 2019 to 2029, compared with 4% growth projected for other job opportunities. Software engineering and web developing are projected to grow 22% and 8%, respectively.

questions.stem: Which role collaborates with end-users to provide technical assistance and support for hardware, software, and technical issues such as access problems, slow performance, and connection problems?
questions.explanation: A technical support specialist collaborates with end-users to provide technical assistance and support for hardware, software, and technical issues. Common issues include inability to access data, slow performance, inefficient software, and connection problems.

questions.stem: Which role writes code that turns software designs into instructions a computer's operating system can follow, and checks the program for errors until it is error-free?
questions.explanation: A computer programmer is responsible for creating the code for operating systems and software applications. After software developers design a program, programmers write code that turns that design into instructions the operating system can follow, then check for errors and rewrite until error-free.

questions.stem: Which role designs and develops websites and website applications, integrates security measures, implements features, and manages site functionality?
questions.explanation: A web developer designs and develops websites and website applications. Using various web technologies and programming languages, they integrate security measures, implement application features, and manage site functionality.

questions.stem: Which role works in partnership with clients to help them use IT to overcome problems or achieve business objectives and improve IT system efficiency?
questions.explanation: An IT consultant works in partnership with clients, helping them utilize information technology to overcome problems or achieve business objectives. They often work to improve the efficiency and structure of IT systems in various organizations.

questions.stem: Which role oversees a company's computer systems, researches and installs networks, assesses system functionality and user needs, and directs analysts, support specialists, and developers?
questions.explanation: An information systems manager is responsible for overseeing a company's computer systems. They research and install new networks and systems, assess system functionality and user needs, and implement technology that directs the work of analysts, support specialists, developers, and other computer-related workers.

questions.stem: Which role oversees the developmental process of a video game and is expected to have a passion for video games and proficiency in languages such as C# and C++?
questions.explanation: A game developer oversees the developmental process of a video game. They may design games or use existing designs and write code that brings characters, environments, and other elements to life. They are expected to have a passion for video games and proficiency in languages such as C# and C++.

questions.stem: Which role stores and organizes company data such as shipping records, payroll data, and financial numbers, and ensures it is secure from corruption, loss, and unauthorized access?
questions.explanation: A database administrator uses specialized applications to store and organize a company's data, such as customer shipping records, payroll data, and confidential financial numbers. They ensure data is available and kept secure from accidental corruption or loss and unauthorized access.

questions.stem: Which role creates flowcharts and models that tell computer programmers how to create code, and participates in designing, constructing, maintaining, and testing software?
questions.explanation: A software developer creates various kinds of software for different applications. They spend much of their time creating flowcharts and models that tell computer programmers how to create code, and they participate in all aspects of software development, including designing, constructing, maintaining, and testing.

questions.stem: Which role analyzes raw data and synthesizes it into understandable results using machine learning, statistics, and programming to gain insights and support business decisions?
questions.explanation: A data scientist analyzes raw data and synthesizes it into results that can easily be understood. They use machine learning, statistics, and programming to analyze data and gain insights for better business decisions.

questions.stem: Which challenge refers to schools not having the same equipment and materials as the industry, resulting in lower chances of employment, and is addressed through free seminars, online trainings, and focused self-study?
questions.explanation: Slow skills development happens because schools in the Philippines that offer the degree do not have the same equipment and materials for students to explore and practice the industry, which can result in a lower chance of employment. Students can attend free seminars and trainings, self-study, and focus on one or two skills to master.

questions.stem: Which challenge describes many applicants competing for the same role, where an impressive resume and skills plus interviews and personality fit matter?
questions.explanation: Competitive job opportunities mean many applicants vie for the same role. An impressive resume and extensive skill set are factors, but so are interviews; HR also looks at personality, manners, and fit with the current environment. Clear communication and displayed interest can make a candidate stand out.

questions.stem: Which statement about Computer Engineering's role in technological advancement is supported by the handout?
options: It is limited to repairing computers
It has been at the forefront of every major technological advancement in the last century, from the Internet and smartphones to robotics
It is unrelated to space exploration
It has only recently become relevant with social media
questions.explanation: Computer Engineering has been at the forefront of every major technological advancement in the last century. From the Internet, smartphones, and automated devices to robotics, it has revolutionized everyone's lifestyle.

questions.stem: What example shows the stakes of computer engineering when done right and when done wrong?
options: It built the first hospitals and then closed them
It invented the Internet and then banned it
It helped put people on the moon with less computing power than today, while errors caused two commercial airlines to crash after takeoff
It created the first legal system and then abolished it
questions.explanation: When done right, computer engineering has put people on the moon with less computing power than today. When done wrong, it caused two commercial airlines to tragically crash into the ground after takeoff.

questions.stem: What problem has held back the industrial Internet of Things (IoT) in smart factories?
options: The limited energy supply of sensors and the short lifetimes of their batteries
questions.explanation: The industrial IoT holds a lot of promise but has been held back because of the limited energy supply of sensors and the short lifetimes of their batteries. Everactive developed sensors that can run nonstop for over 20 years with minimal maintenance.

questions.stem: Why are VR and AR considered prime candidates for the future of remote work?
options: They eliminate the need for the Internet
They replace all computers with paper
They can give users a virtual experience as visual and immersive as a physical one, facilitating collaboration, education, and spontaneity
questions.explanation: VR and AR are prime candidates for evolving remote work. By giving users a virtual experience as visual and immersive as a physical one, computer engineers hope to facilitate collaboration, education, and spontaneity.

questions.stem: What strict requirements must computer engineers meet when designing self-driving cars?
options: Safety and reliability, high-powered sensors, intuitive human-computer interaction, and multiple backups
questions.explanation: Enabling vehicles with elevated levels of autonomy requires meeting strict requirements around safety and reliability. Computer engineers must design vehicles with high-powered sensors, intuitive human-computer interaction, and multiple backups readily available.

questions.stem: What could Automated Lane Keeping Systems (ALKS) potentially prevent over the next decade?
questions.explanation: Automated Lane Keeping Systems (ALKS), currently rolled out in some everyday cars, could prevent an estimated 47,000 serious accidents over the next decade.

questions.stem: What did NASA's Perseverance rover carry when it landed on Mars on February 18, 2021?
questions.explanation: NASA's Perseverance rover landed successfully on Mars on February 18, 2021, with a unique passenger: Ingenuity, the Mars Helicopter. NASA's computer engineers in Southern California built Ingenuity to fly in atmospheric conditions specific to the red planet.

questions.stem: Why was Ingenuity programmed to pilot itself and make its own decisions?
options: Because NASA wanted to test a video game
Because of delays inherent in interplanetary communication
Because it was controlled by students
questions.explanation: Due to the delays inherent in interplanetary communication, Ingenuity has been programmed to pilot itself and even make its own decisions. Back on Earth, computer engineers watch and wait.

questions.stem: How is GPT-3 described in the handout?
options: A Philippine law on data privacy
A Mars helicopter built by NASA
The most powerful form of autocomplete ever invented, built by OpenAI
A self-driving car developed by Microsoft
questions.explanation: Built by OpenAI, GPT-3 is described as the most powerful form of autocomplete ever invented. Users have used it to create question-based search engines, generate programming code, compose music, and respond to medical queries.

questions.stem: Which statement about GPT-3 is accurate according to the handout?
options: It is not perfect and produces several obvious mistakes, but it could automate processes, revolutionize programming, and lead to AI breakthroughs if applied correctly
It is perfect and never makes mistakes
It was built by the Council of Europe
questions.explanation: GPT-3 is not perfect. For every astounding success, it produces several obvious mistakes. But if applied correctly, it could automate a substantial number of processes, revolutionize computer programming, and lead to important breakthroughs in AI research.

questions.stem: Which guideline suggests planning computer/IT projects for the common good, such as projects for underprivileged groups, water saving, electricity, or mental health?
options: Plan projects with an attitude and intention of creating systems and devices for the common good
questions.explanation: Planning projects with an intention of creating systems and devices for the common good directs focus on achieving morally correct outputs instead of distractions caused by ill-intentioned motives. Examples include projects for underprivileged groups, water saving, electricity, and mental health.

questions.stem: Which guideline emphasizes integrity and ethics, keeping the work environment free from conflicts, and practicing professionalism when creating outputs?
questions.explanation: Professionalism is not just about qualifications and skills but also about integrity and ethics. Practicing professionalism affects everyone involved in a project and helps keep the work environment free from conflicts, supporting collaboration.

questions.stem: Which guideline encourages computer engineers to be pioneers and inventors, create next trends, take risks, and aim for innovations that make society function better?
questions.explanation: Computer engineers are pioneers and inventors in nature and are expected to create the next trends in technology. Aiming for bigger technological innovations helps fulfill their social responsibilities. It does not have to be revolutionary all the time, just relevant and able to make society function better.

questions.stem: Which guideline encourages creative alternatives, avoiding electronic waste, not relying on existing programs altered to pass as original, and buying used working sensors or processors?
questions.explanation: Thinking outside the box means using a creative mind to come up with smart alternatives for new systems and using computer materials that prevent the growth of electronic waste. It also means not relying on existing programs altered to pass as original, and buying used working sensors or processors with the same capabilities as new ones.

questions.stem: Which guideline requires reporting blatant motivations that cross what is morally correct, and complying with rules and admitting faults if you are the one reported?
questions.explanation: Be observant means not letting camaraderie stop you from reporting blatant motivations crossing what is morally correct, such as creating systems and devices that are harmful and illegal. If you are the one reported, comply with rules and procedures and admit your faults.
